node.label: Richard Hofstadter
node.date_label: Social Darwinism in American Thought (1944) · The American Political Tradition (1948) · The Age of Reform (1955)
node.description: A historian of American political culture whose interpretations moved from economic-interest explanations toward ideas, status anxieties and political irrationality. Eric Foner’s retrospective distinguishes his critical account of consensus from celebratory consensus history and also identifies its limits.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Social Darwinism in American Thought (1944); The American Political Tradition (1948); The Age of Reform (1955).

incident_edges.relationship: Critically reworks the economic-conflict interpretation and explores ideological consensus in American politics.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Foner distinguishes Hofstadter’s critical consensus interpretation from celebratory versions and notes the later reconsideration of conflict.

incident_edges.relationship: Brings status anxiety, symbols and irrationality into accounts of political culture.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Foner’s named substantive reading also judges the treatment of Populists and Progressives exaggerated and elitist in important respects. This qualification survives the contribution arrow.

incident_edges.relationship: Hofstadter criticizes Turner’s weak critical response to expansion, Indigenous dispossession and anti-Mexican and anti-Chinese nativism, as quoted by Bogue (1994).
incident_edges.evidence_note: Bogue 206 and 220n 38 visually checked. His quotation identifies The Progressive Historians,104,106 in a 1969 manifestation. Hofstadter’s original chapter and 1949 essay remain unread; the claim is expressly mediated by Bogue.

incident_edges.relationship: Joint conception of the Oxford History of the United States provides a shared editorial project.
incident_edges.evidence_note: McPherson’s2000 recollection names both as conceiving a multiauthor series modelled on the Oxford History of England. Undirected editorial overlap, without causal priority or a shared interpretation of every subject. The transcript’s Hofstetter spelling is a variant, not a second historian.

incident_edges.relationship: As Foner recounts, defends the Populists’ corporate critique against Hofstadter’s emphasis on conspiracy and cultural hatreds.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Explicit named scholarly mediation: Foner’s2022 review, paragraphs beginning For decades and It was a book, distinguishes their disagreement from friendship. It also notes Woodward later conceded exaggerating white Populists’ racial egalitarianism. Original exchanges and complete books remain unread; editorial collaboration does not erase this disagreement.

incident_edges.relationship: Rodgers disputes Hofstadter’s relatively prosperous framing of the Progressive Era, foregrounding acute labor crisis and conflict over corporate power.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1982 essay120 and note33 explicitly contrasts Hofstadter’s framing with recent labor history. David Montgomery,Bruno Ramirez and Richard Edwards retain the supporting works’ separate credit. Rodgers also treats Hofstadter’s generation as having brilliantly launched a historiographical question at114; disagreement does not erase that assessment. The original Age of Reform and all cited labor books remain unread.

incident_edges.relationship: In Garrett Epps’s reading, Davis adapts Hofstadter’s paranoid-style concept to antebellum Slave Power arguments.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Explicit named scholarly mediation, Epps2004p186, not fresh reading of Davis1969 or Hofstadter. Epps also criticizes Davis for conflating fringe conspiracy claims with sober constitutional arguments; his objection remains attributed and is held for missing Epps endpoint. A bounded conceptual resource, not endorsement of the diagnosis of abolitionists.

incident_edges.relationship: Bederman includes Hofstadter’s Social Darwinism in American Thought among the historiographic resources for her account of Darwinism’s American reception and its tensions with Protestant millennial expectations.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Body26 describes educated Americans understanding Darwinism through conflict and survival without the older providential telos. Note102 directs readers to Hofstadter’s1955 edition alongside Robert C. Bannister1979 and Cynthia Eagle Russett1976 for Darwinism’s reception in the United States. This is a particular plural historical resource, not personal formation or wholesale adoption of Hofstadter’s interpretation. Originals unread. The separate self-employment statistic at12/n45 carries no additional interpretive claim.

incident_edges.relationship: Wood uses Hofstadter’s description of conspiratorial explanation as personal causation to develop his own historical account.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1982 essay explicitly takes up Hofstadter’s account of deliberate individual will when analyzing eighteenth-century causal assumptions. This conceptual use coexists with a challenge to its application across periods. Wood preserves possible modern applicability at his conclusion; full Hofstadter book unread.

incident_edges.relationship: Wood challenges extending Hofstadter’s pathological and marginal model to widespread eighteenth-century beliefs.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1982 distinguishes Hofstadter’s expressly metaphorical usage from clinical diagnosis and acknowledges that Hofstadter omitted the Revolution. Wood argues that contemporary rational causality made conspiratorial beliefs broadly intelligible, while allowing a different modern assessment at441. This is a contextual limit, not rejection of all Hofstadter’s analysis.

incident_edges.relationship: Uses Hofstadter’s bill-of-lading characterization as a rhetorical foil in discussing the Emancipation Proclamation.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own scanned1996 essay30 reuses the attributed description;2001 Q&A qualifies its implication by emphasizing extraordinary effects despite flat wording. The speech calls it moral impact, whereas scanned essay says moral grandeur; do not silently merge as a verified original quotation. Original Hofstadter passage unread. This resource does not imply agreement that proclamation lacked political force.

incident_edges.relationship: Lears uses Hofstadter’s critique of the entrepreneurial consensus to frame how dissent can share dominant cultural commitments.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own576praises analytical insight but expressly denies making Hofstadter a Gramscian after the fact. The American Political Tradition1948 is cited atn19; the distinct Populism criticism concerns Age of Reform1955. Originals unread.

incident_edges.relationship: Lears questions Hofstadter’s dismissal of Populism and failure to grasp efforts to build cultural alternatives.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own576contrasts Age of Reform’s agrarian-myth account with Lawrence Goodwyn’s reconstruction, retaining Goodwyn’s credit. His positive appraisal of Hofstadter’s entrepreneurial-consensus analysis remains separate.

incident_edges.relationship: McPherson names Hofstadter as a formative model for historical writing that reaches academic and interested lay audiences.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own recollection explicitly joins Hofstadter with Allan Nevins and Arthur Schlesinger Jr.; all retain credit. This is a writing/audience influence during graduate school and after, not evidence that McPherson adopted consensus historiography or a specified Hofstadter book. No original reading of those authors in this dossier.

records.context: Examines common assumptions through critical, selective portraits of political leaders; shared premises do not remove every conflict.
